records.sourceLabel: SSRN exact paper record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The paper constructs a labelled dataset of 2,082 Mafia-connected Italian firms from judicial evidence and applies gradient-boosted classification to financial-statement information. The abstract reports hold-out performance of 75.8% AUC and 90.4% precision, using accounting patterns to identify criminal connections.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact SSRN title/authors/DOI record and located the direct 50-page PDF. The synopsis is abstract_only; the full-text locator is stored separately in retrieval_coverage.csv. No verbatim abstract or model-derived scientific decision is persisted here.

records.synopsis: The article links mafia presence to concentration in Sicily's construction market and evaluates two anti-mafia interventions, finding that firm seizure and reassignment can weaken criminal organisations' dominant economic positions and increase local competition.
records.note: Exact title and DOI 10.1007/s11187-019-00250-w matched the queue candidate and SciSpace exposed an abstract. Scite independently confirmed the exact bibliographic record but did not expose an abstract in its result. No abstract text is persisted here.

records.synopsis: The article develops a framework for mafia territorial expansion and applies it to Germany, finding a particularly strong 'Ndrangheta presence and an expansion pattern centred more on economic infiltration and illegal markets than on reproducing home-territory embeddedness.
records.note: Exact title and DOI 10.1007/s10611-013-9473-7 matched the queue candidate. SciSpace exposed the published abstract and Scite independently exposed an abstract-bearing exact DOI record. No abstract text is persisted here.

records.synopsis: The article estimates the effects of judicial administration on Italian criminal firms over 2004–2016 and reports deterioration in profitability and efficiency together with higher leverage after criminal management is removed, highlighting the difficulty of re-establishing viable market-based governance.
records.note: Exact title and DOI 10.1007/s11187-020-00439-4 matched the queue candidate and SciSpace exposed the published abstract. Scite confirmed the bibliographic identity but its abstract field was contaminated by repository licensing text and was therefore not used as abstract evidence. No abstract text is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: American Economic Association publisher record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The article studies firm-level effects of Mafia infiltration by combining investigative records with panel data on governance and balance sheets. It reports that targeted firms tend to be young and less efficient and that infiltration is associated with higher revenues without proportional input growth, alongside worsening financial conditions and eventual market exit.
records.note: Parallel Search located and fetched the exact AEA DOI/title/authors publisher record. The synopsis uses the verified publisher abstract only (abstract_only); the existing retrieval ledger already records the publisher full-text PDF. No abstract text is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: RePEc/CEPR abstract record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The paper develops a framework for distinguishing organised-crime groups’ motives for infiltrating legal firms and validates it with new Italian Financial Intelligence Unit data. The abstract estimates that about 2% of Italian firms have links with organised crime and distinguishes three principal infiltration motives.
records.note: Parallel Search verified the 2024 title/authors on the RePEc CEPR record and located an exact full-text IZA manifestation at EconStor, recorded separately in retrieval_coverage.csv. This synopsis is abstract_only; no full text or verbatim abstract is committed and versions are not silently canonicalised.

records.sourceLabel: CORE full-text dissertation located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The dissertation develops an accounting-oriented study of criminal firms, defined as apparently legal businesses controlled by people connected to organised crime. Its structure includes research on organisational roles within criminal firms and a machine-learning approach to detecting them from firm information.
records.note: Parallel Search verified the exact University of Padua repository record and fetched the CORE full-text manifestation; its title page identifies Francesco Ambrosini and the dissertation title, and its contents expose the organisational-role and detection studies. Evidence basis: full_text. No scientific eligibility or canonical-identity decision is inferred, and the connector read is not treated as governed private full-text ingestion.

records.sourceLabel: University of Palermo institutional repository abstract located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The chapter studies continuity-preserving Italian preventive measures—judicial administration under Article 34 and judicial control under Article 34-bis—through an organisational-resilience lens. It uses a comparative multi-case analysis of 11 firms to examine changes in operating and financial conditions around the interventions.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact institutional repository record, matching title, Giovanni Scire' and Enzo Bivona, year 2026, and an explicit Abstract section. Evidence basis: abstract_only. No open full-text manifestation was verified in this pass, so claims beyond the repository abstract remain not_verifiable.

records.sourceLabel: University of Milan CROSS article and full-text manifestation located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The article examines why organised crime infiltrates public procurement, how infiltration techniques have evolved across the phases of contracting, and how the legal and regulatory response developed in parallel.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact University of Milan publisher article for DOI 10.13130/cross-7791 and the direct scholarly full-text manifestation, matching Sara Spartà and the 2016 CROSS issue. Evidence basis: full_text; the synopsis is a conservative paraphrase of the verified author abstract. No verbatim article text or scientific decision is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: IFS 2023 working-paper PDF located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The working paper exploits variation in firms’ exposure to Covid-19 closure days as a shock to revenues and financial conditions to estimate whether distress raises Mafia infiltration risk. It reports that worsening financial conditions increased infiltration likelihood, while government support partly offset the effect; heterogeneity is consistent with a role for Mafia lending when firms face temporary debt-repayment difficulties.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact IFS 2023 working-paper manifestation, matching Marco Castelluccio, Lucia Rizzica and the candidate title/year. Evidence basis: full_text. A later Bank of Italy Temi di discussione no. 1502 (2025) manifestation was also located but is not silently substituted for or canonicalised with the 2023 candidate. No verbatim text or scientific decision is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: RAND Europe exact report record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The report examines serious and organised crime infiltration of legitimate European businesses and maps risk relevant to the interaction between criminal activity and the legal economy. It is an EU-level risk-mapping study rather than evidence from a single firm or locality.
records.note: Parallel Search matched the exact title, authors and DOI 10.2837/64101 on RAND Europe and resolved the DOI to the official EU Publications Office record, which lists an English PDF. Evidence basis: partial_text from authoritative report summary and publication metadata; the report body was not fetched in this pass, so methods, variables and findings beyond that support remain not_verifiable.

records.sourceLabel: SSRN exact abstract record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The paper conceptualises public financial-management systems as diagnostic infrastructures whose budgeting, accounting and procurement routines can reveal behavioural drift when institutional integrity erodes. It uses Italian municipalities dissolved for Mafia infiltration under Law 164/1991 as the empirical setting for examining that drift.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact SSRN title and four-author record for the 33-page paper, first posted 6 May 2025 and later revised. Evidence basis: abstract_only. The paper body was not used in this pass, so methods, variables and findings not explicit in the SSRN abstract remain not_verifiable; no scientific decision is persisted.

records.sourceLabel: Bristol University Press OA chapter located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The chapter argues for studying criminal infiltration of the legal economy beyond a mafia-specific lens. It frames infiltration around the channelling of resources and the exertion of control by organised-crime actors within legal businesses and discusses why the research agenda should extend beyond traditional mafia-type organisations.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the authoritative Bristol University Press full-text chapter and publisher XML, matching Giovanni Nicolazzo, the exact title, publication date and pages 111–124. Evidence basis: full_text. The publisher record assigns DOI 10.51952/9781529247145.ch007, while the current review record carries 10.56687/9781529247145-010; this identifier conflict is preserved explicitly and requires separate metadata reconciliation. The OA locator is not treated as authority to overwrite the registered DOI or canonical identity, and no scientific decision is persisted.

records.sourceLabel: Oxford University Research Archive thesis record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The thesis asks why and how mafias expand to new territories, when they engage in governance rather than trading activities, and when expansion fails. It tests theory-derived hypotheses against three case studies of the 'Ndrangheta in Germany using hard-to-reach sources including judicial data, intelligence reports and archival material.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact Oxford repository record matching Zora Lea Hauser, 2022 and the PhD-thesis title. Evidence basis: abstract_only for this synopsis. ORA also lists a 3.2 MB dissemination-version PDF, but the connector did not expose a stable direct file URL in this pass, so the existing source-only retrieval locator is not promoted to full_text automatically; substantive claims beyond the ORA abstract remain not_verifiable.
